# KBD constraints — prometheus-skills-mini

Generated by `/kbd-init` on 2026-09-21; command fields regenerated by `/kbd-init --force` on
2026-09-21 after `project-scaffold` and `platform-spawn` landed. That regeneration is kbd-init's
own job, not a change editing its gates — the ownership table below distinguishes the two. The
`openspec validate …` form it replaced could never have run on Windows: npm installs the CLI as
`openspec.cmd`, which Node cannot start without a shell. `AGENTS.md` has no "Never Do" section, so the blocking rules are
derived from its §P project block and §A constitution, and from the hard constraints in
`openspec/config.yaml`. Each rule names its source.

## Command policy (applies to every `check:`, `command:` and `target:` below)

This project forbids telling an agent to run `grep`, `sed`, `jq`, `awk`, `curl`, `mktemp` or `chmod`, and
requires every command to behave the same from `cmd.exe`, Windows PowerShell 5.1, bash and zsh. So:

- Content checks use **`git grep --no-index --exclude-standard`** — `git` is a permitted dependency, it is a
  native Windows executable, and `--no-index` works whether or not the directory is a git repository.
  Pathspecs such as `"lib/*.mjs"` are recursive. **A match is a violation**: exit 0 = violations printed,
  exit 1 = clean.
- Double quotes only. No `&&`, `||` or `;` chaining — Windows PowerShell 5.1 rejects `&&`. Steps that must run
  in sequence are separate entries.
- `[$]` stands for a literal dollar sign so the pattern means the same thing inside and outside a POSIX shell.
- Every check below was run against known-bad fixtures at generation time and matched exactly the intended
  lines. No mandatory command wrapper, toolchain selector or external storage path is declared by this
  project, so there is no prefix to propagate. If a `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` policy is ever adopted, it must be
  added to every compiling command here.

## Path ownership — hidden does not mean disposable

| Path | Owner | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/rules/`, `.cursor/rules/`, `docs/skill-routing.md` | `rules/build.mjs` | Generated. Edit `rules/src/`, then rebuild. A hand edit fails `build-passes`. |
| `.claude/skills/openspec-*`, `.claude/commands/opsx/`, `.agents/skills/openspec-*`, `.cursor/commands/`, `.cursor/skills/`, `.opencode/` | OpenSpec CLI | Refresh with `openspec update`; do not hand-edit. |
| `.kbd-orchestrator/project.json` — everything except `activePhase` | `/kbd-init` ONLY | Never written by a change. Command fields are derived from `package.json` scripts; re-run `/kbd-init --force` after they change. |
| `.kbd-orchestrator/project.json` — `activePhase` | `/kbd-new-phase`, `/kbd-next-phase` | Step 7 of those skills flips it at a phase bracket. Under runtime authority the runtime projects the waypoint and the phase directory but NOT this field, so the skill still writes it. A change never touches it. |
| `.kbd-orchestrator/constraints.md` — rules and thresholds | `/kbd-init` | A change never loosens, deletes or adds a RULE here. |
| `.kbd-orchestrator/constraints.md` — a `check:` expression | a change, with evidence | Permitted ONLY to fix a demonstrated false positive, and only when the change ALSO proves the corrected check still catches a real violation. Every such edit is called out in its own commit and in the change's tasks. Three exist (see below); each was a check matching prose rather than code. |
| `.kbd-orchestrator/phases/**` | KBD stages | Written by the stage that owns them. |
| `.prometheus/` | Karpathy logging / memory | Append-only and dated. Entries are marked superseded, never deleted. |
| `openspec/changes/archive/` | OpenSpec | History. Never rewritten. |
| `/Users/gqadonis/Projects/prometheus/prometheus-skill-pack` | another repository | Reference only (`project.json` → `workspace`). **Never written**, including its worktrees. |

### Check expressions corrected by a change

| Constraint | False positive it matched | Proof it still discriminates |
|---|---|---|
| `no-home-or-tmp-literals` | a comment in `lib/platform/paths.mjs` naming `$HOME` while explaining the rule | `process.env.HOME` added to a code line is reported |
| (reverted) `no-home-or-tmp-literals` v2 | — | a `grep` pipe was used, which this project forbids and Windows lacks; reverted to the plain form |
| (reverted) `os-locations-only-via-platform` | — | a TIGHTENING, not a loosening: the check reported clean over four real `scripts/` violations. The corrected pattern was verified by execution, but applying it required a rule authorising check tightenings, and a change writing its own authorisation is the same circularity as widening a gate to fit its own code. Reverted; the false negative is documented in the constraint's `note:` and left for the rule owner |

One correction remains (`no-home-or-tmp-literals`), and it is not circular: the text it excuses is a
COMMENT IN THE RULE'S OWN SUBJECT — `lib/platform/paths.mjs` cannot explain why nothing else may read
a home location without naming what it forbids. A second correction was reverted after review pointed
out the circularity: a test fixture had tripped `no-console-log-in-lib`, and widening the check to
excuse it was loosening a gate to fit my own code. The fixture was changed instead, and the original
check restored. That is the standard: change the code, not the gate.

## Blocking constraints (prevent archiving until resolved)

```yaml
constraints:
  - id: build-passes
    severity: blocking
    source: 'AGENTS.md pointer block; openspec/config.yaml (rules v4)'
    description: 'Generated agent rules match rules/src/ and stay inside the Layer 0 / Layer 1 budgets'
    command: 'npm run check'

  - id: tests-pass
    severity: blocking
    source: 'openspec/config.yaml conventions'
    description: 'The node:test suite passes'
    command: 'npm test'

  - id: specs-valid
    severity: blocking
    source: 'AGENTS.md §P — OpenSpec is the spec backend'
    description: 'All OpenSpec specs and active changes validate'
    command: 'npm run spec:validate'

  - id: no-shell-or-python-files
    severity: blocking
    source: 'AGENTS.md §P — Node.js LTS is the only script runtime'
    description: 'No .sh, .bash, .py or .ps1 file anywhere in the repository'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -l -e "" -- "*.sh" "*.bash" "*.py" "*.ps1" ":!tools/prometheus-knowledge"'
    note: 'One pathspec exclusion, added 2026-09-21 when the operator directed that the Rust pk CLI be vendored as a submodule at tools/prometheus-knowledge: that repository carries scripts/pk-lint-cron.sh and scripts/pmpo-reflect.sh. They are upstream files this project neither authors nor runs, and --no-index scans the working tree, so without the exclusion a vendored checkout fails a rule about what THIS project ships. The pattern is unchanged; proof it still discriminates: a .sh created anywhere else, including directly under tools/, is reported. A .ps1 is admissible only beside a cross-platform equivalent, and only through an OpenSpec change that says why Node cannot do the job. Then scope this check; do not delete it.'

  - id: no-shell-true
    severity: blocking
    source: '.claude/rules/node-scripts.md — Processes'
    description: 'Child processes are spawned with shell: false and an args array'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -E -e "shell: *true" -- "lib/*.mjs" "scripts/*.mjs" "hooks/*.mjs" "rules/*.mjs"'

  - id: no-home-or-tmp-literals
    severity: blocking
    source: '.claude/rules/node-scripts.md — Paths'
    description: 'Paths come from os.homedir() / os.tmpdir() / path.join, never $HOME, process.env.HOME or /tmp'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -E -e "[$]HOME|process\.env\.HOME|/tmp/" -- "lib/*.mjs" "scripts/*.mjs" "hooks/*.mjs" "rules/*.mjs"'
    note: 'Back to the original -E form, with no pipe and no PCRE. An earlier attempt to exempt comments used a grep pipe (forbidden by the command policy, and grep is absent on stock Windows) and then git grep -P (PCRE is a build-time option, so the check could error on another machine). Neither is needed: the comment that triggered this now describes the forbidden spellings instead of quoting them, so the plain check passes. Prose that must quote a literal belongs in a .md file, which this pathspec does not cover.'

  - id: os-locations-only-via-platform
    severity: blocking
    source: '.claude/rules/node-scripts.md — Paths; adversarial review of platform-paths-and-text'
    description: 'Only lib/platform/paths.mjs asks the OS where things live; every other module and test uses the helpers'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -E -e "os\.(tmpdir|homedir)\(\)" -- "lib/*.mjs" "scripts/*.mjs" "hooks/*.mjs" "rules/*.mjs" ":!lib/platform/paths.mjs" ":!lib/platform/paths.test.mjs"'
    note: 'paths.test.mjs is the single documented exception: it asserts that the DEFAULT helpers delegate to the real OS, which cannot be asserted through the helper without becoming a tautology. Review caught two modules reading os.tmpdir() directly; this check makes the next one mechanical. KNOWN FALSE NEGATIVE, left in place deliberately and awaiting the rule owner: this pattern matches only the `os.tmpdir()` member-call spelling, so `import { tmpdir } from "node:os"` (and `require`/`await import` of the same specifier) is invisible to it. Four such violations stand today — scripts/convert-htmx-pdf.mjs:18, scripts/design-svg-logo.mjs:36, scripts/hook-cold-start.mjs:13, scripts/refine-moodboard.mjs:45 — and the check reports clean over them. Adding `-e "node:os"` fixes it, and was verified by execution to run, to report all four, and to match import/require/await-import in a probe. It is NOT applied here because this table authorises a change to edit a check only to fix a demonstrated FALSE POSITIVE; a tightening has no clause, and adding one would be a change writing its own authorisation. Found by rounds 6 and 7 of the review-housekeeping diff review; reverted in round 8. Needs /kbd-init or an explicit operator decision.'

  - id: no-zeespec
    severity: blocking
    source: 'AGENTS.md §P — there is no ZeeSpec'
    description: 'No skill, hook, script or library references ZeeSpec or reads .zeespec/'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -i -e "zeespec" -- "skills/*" "lib/*" "hooks/*" "scripts/*" "templates/*"'

  - id: no-hardcoded-secrets
    severity: blocking
    source: 'AGENTS.md A-3; .claude/rules/docker-services.md — Compose rules'
    description: 'No inline database credentials or provider keys in code, config or Compose files'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -E -e "--(user|pass)=" -e "sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}" -- "docker/*" "*.mjs" "*.json" "*.toml" "*.yaml" "*.yml"'
    note: 'Credentials reach containers through env_file / ${VAR} from a git-ignored docker/.env. Markdown is excluded on purpose: the docs quote the source pack''s root/root as the thing not to do.'

  - id: compose-ports-loopback-only
    severity: blocking
    source: '.claude/rules/docker-services.md — Compose rules (A-3: a real boundary)'
    description: 'Every published port is bound to 127.0.0.1'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -E -e "- +.?[0-9]+:[0-9]+.? *$" -- "docker/*.yaml" "docker/*.yml"'

  - id: no-console-log-in-lib
    severity: blocking
    source: '.claude/rules/node-scripts.md — Structure (I/O lives at the edge)'
    description: 'Library modules do not print. Entry points under scripts/, hooks/ and rules/build.mjs may.'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -E -e "console\.(log|debug)" -- "lib/*.mjs" "rules/lib/*.mjs"'

  - id: no-symlinks
    severity: blocking
    source: 'AGENTS.md §P — no symlinks'
    description: 'No symbolic links in the repository; installers copy; AGENTS.md is a generated copy'
    note: 'No portable one-line check exists without a forbidden tool. Manual until scripts/doctor.mjs lands (OpenSpec change installer-and-doctor); then replace this note with its command.'

  - id: exactly-two-services
    severity: blocking
    source: 'AGENTS.md §P — exactly two services exist'
    description: 'docker/compose.yaml defines surrealdb, surreal-memory and liter-llm only; no other daemon, database or listening port is added'
    note: 'Manual review. A third service needs its own OpenSpec proposal that says why.'

  - id: reference-repo-untouched
    severity: blocking
    source: 'project.json workspace roles'
    description: 'Nothing under prometheus-skill-pack (the port source) is created, modified or deleted'
    note: 'Manual review of the change''s file list.'
```

## Warning constraints (acknowledge before archiving)

```yaml
  - id: tests-for-new-features
    severity: warning
    source: 'openspec/config.yaml conventions — tests written first'
    description: 'Every new module under lib/ has a node:test file that was seen to fail before it passed'

  - id: no-forbidden-tools-in-instructions
    severity: warning
    source: 'AGENTS.md §P — never tell an agent to run jq, sed, grep, awk, curl, mktemp or chmod'
    description: 'SKILL.md and command files do not instruct agents to run POSIX-only tools'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -E -e "(^|[^A-Za-z])(jq|sed|awk|curl|mktemp|chmod) " -- "skills/*.md" "hooks/*" "templates/*"'
    note: 'The rule itself is blocking; the check is a heuristic and can match prose, so it is a warning that demands a human look at each hit. `grep` is left out of the pattern because `git grep` is the sanctioned replacement and would match.'

  - id: no-stub-comments
    severity: warning
    source: 'kbd generic template'
    description: 'No TODO/FIXME/STUB/HACK comments in committed code'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -E -e "TODO|FIXME|STUB|HACK" -- "lib/*.mjs" "scripts/*.mjs" "hooks/*.mjs" "rules/*.mjs" ":!scripts/convert-htmx-react.mjs"'
    note: 'One exclusion, and it is a pathspec rather than a weakened pattern, so the rule still applies in full to every file this project authors. scripts/convert-htmx-react.mjs:308 EMITS "/* TODO: convert: ... */" into the React it generates, alongside a structured ambiguousRegions entry, so a human can see which Alpine expressions need manual rewriting. That is output data, not an unfinished stub, and deleting it would silently drop information the converter exists to surface. Proof it still discriminates: adding a real TODO comment to any other file under these pathspecs is reported.'

  - id: file-under-500-lines
    severity: warning
    source: 'AGENTS.md §P — no code file over 500 lines'
    description: 'No code file exceeds 500 physical lines; partition by responsibility, never by line count'
    note: 'Manual until a Node line-count check exists. Exemptions only in rules/line-limit-allowlist.txt, and only for generated or vendored files.'

  - id: services-degrade
    severity: warning
    source: 'AGENTS.md §P — everything must still work with both services down'
    description: 'A change touching lib/memory or lib/review was exercised with the containers stopped; service-touching hooks exit 0'
    note: 'Manual. Starting Docker is tier T3 and never belongs in a workflow trigger.'

  - id: windows-verified
    severity: warning
    source: 'README §9 — open questions'
    description: 'Behaviour claimed for Windows was run on Windows, or the completion summary says it was not (A-6)'
    note: 'Until the three-OS CI matrix exists (OpenSpec change platform-foundation), every Windows claim made from macOS is self-reported.'
```

Dropped from the generic template, with reasons: `no-any-type` (no TypeScript here), `accessibility-basics`
(no UI), `no-unused-imports` and `no-lint-warnings` (no linter is configured; `lint_command` is `null` — add
them back in the change that introduces one).

## Workflow triggers

```yaml
workflow_triggers:
  - event: on_iteration_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: 'npm run check'

  - event: on_change_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: 'npm test'

  - event: on_change_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: 'npm run spec:validate'

  - event: on_refinement_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: 'git add -A'

  - event: on_refinement_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: 'git commit -m "kbd: refine <change-id>" -m "Assisted-by: <AGENT>:<MODEL> [<tools>]"'
```

Notes on the last two: they are separate entries because of the no-chaining policy. The `Assisted-by` trailer
is required by A-15, and `Signed-off-by` must never be added. They commit locally only — nothing here pushes,
files or publishes (A-16). The repository was initialized on 2026-09-20 (`git init -b main`); it has no commits
and no remote yet, so these triggers will create the first commits and nothing can be pushed.

# Assessment: unified-tool-approval-authority
Project: prometheus-skills-mini / The Boss / Universal Agent Runtime
Date: 2026-09-24
Stage: assessment only; architecture recommendation, not execution approval.
Verification: source inspection and existing failed integration artifacts. No new tests, builds, or production edits.

## Decision in brief

Keep UAR as the run and approval coordinator and The Boss as the independently authoritative host of its capabilities and user interface. Replace the approval-event-fed bridge credit ledger with an explicit, identity-bound execution admission contract. Do not replace UAR with Codex, embed another harness, or introduce a durable workflow engine to solve this boundary.

However, **the observed Gate V failure is not proof of an approval bypass**. The gate itself sends the wrong filesystem argument. Fixing that fixture and preserving the actual failed tool result is a separate, necessary prerequisite to interpreting its next result. Architecture changes must be justified by the inspected production gaps below, not by treating this malformed invocation as proof of them.

There is no universally perfect architecture or exhaustive list of all harnesses. The recommendation is bounded by this project's split Rust-runtime/Electron-host trust boundary, delivery priorities, and the inspected versions.

## Baseline and cross-tool position

The active worktrees are:
- Boss: /Users/gqadonis/Projects/prometheus/worktrees/the-boss-uar, branch feat/uar-agent-runtime, HEAD 2fa0b4b87f0e8991a97873590d093991b91b395f.
- UAR: /Users/gqadonis/Projects/prometheus/worktrees/uar-the-boss-sidecar, branch feat/the-boss-sidecar, HEAD 19e2ad1575621fcd76d01d16a8ef96aa5751a843.
- Codex reference: /Users/gqadonis/Projects/references/codex, HEAD 986ff1cc7ced0081ec5014b700a376333d87f869.

Both integration worktrees contain uncommitted work. HEAD alone is therefore insufficient provenance; research/local-evidence.json records inspected file hashes and excerpts. The primary UAR checkout and Boss .worktrees/update-agent-team-skills-mini are not this gate's source. In particular, the active Boss connection uses the agent catalog; an older inline-artifact connection must not be described as the current implementation.

At canonical revision 667 this assessment child has 0/0 implementation changes. Its parent integration-administration remains 21/37 tasks, one unfinished registered change; the project roll-up 17/36 is a different counter. No parent task was completed by this assessment. No running native Codex goal was found in the preceding status check. KBD state remains the authoritative process position, not evidence of a native goal.

## What is actually established about the blocker

Existing Gate V error-context.md records: run done, no stream error, approvalCount 0, reattached false, toolOutput false. The second provider request contains a tool-role message. It does not record that message's content or prove a side effect.

Source chain:
1. tests/e2e/gates/uarExperienceGate.test.ts:252 creates the built-in @cherry/filesystem server.
2. Its provider stub selects the first __write tool and sends {path, content} at lines 106–120.
3. src/main/ai/mcp/servers/filesystem/tools/write.ts:8 requires {file_path, content}; line 24 exports that schema.
4. UAR src/llm/orchestrator.rs:2309 validates against the descriptor before the approval gate at 2371. Validation failure emits a failed ToolResult and continues at 2314–2354.
5. The stub treats *any* tool-role message as success and emits “completed after the approved filesystem operation” at lines 105 and 126, irrespective of error content.

The fixture/schema mismatch is confirmed by static inspection. It is a strong causal explanation of zero prompts and a model follow-up without successful tool output. It has NOT been rerun here, and the saved failure lacks the actual tool-error payload; historical causal attribution remains an inference, not a newly reproduced result. Do not claim an unauthorized write occurred. The gate's assertion about the marker file is after the failing assertion and was never reached.

The gate's detach/attach at lines 340–341 detaches the renderer from Boss. It does not disconnect the Boss-to-UAR SSE transport or restart the sidecar. It cannot certify those separate recovery claims. Another saved trace failed during window startup and must not be conflated with this approval failure.

Why the counter stayed at 21: the next task is a broad end-to-end acceptance boundary, so preceding code edits do not advance it. The diagnostic strategy compounded the delay: a malformed fixture, success narration after error results, inadequate retained failure content, confusion between worktrees, and conflation of renderer reconnect with runtime recovery. The evidence does not quantify how much time each contributed or establish that every earlier attempt had the same cause.

## Current authority and data flow

Catalog definition and policy → UAR effective run policy → descriptor validation → governance/approval gate → root-lane pending waiter → custom AG-UI approval event → Boss approval controller → Boss registry/UI → bridge credit plus approval POST → UAR MCP invocation → Boss MCP bridge → actual server.

Sources, relative to the active worktrees:
- UAR runtime/manager.rs:4819–4930 resolves Deny/Ask/Auto and governance. The dirty implementation limits local bypass to Auto. A Cedar denial precedes prompting; Ask is not permission to bypass governance.
- UAR runtime/thread/approvals.rs:23–159 has a root lane, serialized requests, exact approval IDs, oneshot decisions, cancellation and timeout. Child channels share the root lane. Pending continuation state is in memory.
- Boss UarToolApprovalController.ts:139–158 independently recomputes prompt/approve/deny. Built-in auto and permissive Boss modes can approve an incoming UAR Ask event without a person.
- Boss controller:78–85 and 130–135 credits the host ledger before posting the decision, revoking on a request error. There is no atomic shared admission receipt across that HTTP boundary.
- Boss UarHostMcpBridge.ts:133–173 stores call IDs in a queue keyed by tool and argument hash, but consume accepts only tool and arguments and shifts the first ID. Incoming execution does not establish which invocation it consumes.
- UAR mcp/registry.rs:2300–2304 constructs the actual MCP call with name and arguments, without the originating tool-call or approval identity.
- Boss UarRuntimeConnection.ts:233–254 retries the live stream with an existing adapter and replay cursor. UarAguiAdapter.ts retains event deduplication and routes custom approval events. These are useful existing components, not durable restart recovery.

Trust boundaries already present: provider-produced arguments, renderer-to-main decisions, principal/owner-bound UAR APIs, per-run authenticated loopback bridge, mounted-server/workspace authorization, and independent MCP servers. These boundaries justify admission, identity and revocation requirements. They do not justify unrelated platform hardening.

## Gap assessment

| Area | State | Concrete gap / retained strength |
|---|---|---|
| Catalog authority and run ownership | PARTIAL | Active code selects catalog ID/revision and owned run endpoints; preserve this. Do not regress to inline synthetic agents. |
| Effective policy composition | PARTIAL | UAR computes policy, Boss may silently weaken Ask. Conversely UAR Auto may never emit the event that funds the host ledger. |
| Exact invocation admission | PARTIAL | Run-scoped bearer exists; tool+args FIFO cannot distinguish identical calls or root versus child execution identity. |
| Approval UX and registry | PARTIAL | Existing prompt and opaque ID response path is reusable; UI events currently participate in execution authorization and controller errors are not a durable decision state. |
| Validation | DONE for inspected path | Parse/schema validation precedes gate. Current validator returns parsed arguments unchanged, so argument normalization drift is not an observed defect here. |
| Live disconnect/cancellation | PARTIAL | Existing cursor, generation and cancellation machinery; renderer reattachment proves less than SSE reconnect. |
| Process restart | PARTIAL | Pending waiters/bridge grants are memory-only; no inspected contract for reconciliation of a possibly dispatched external effect. |
| Observable failures | PARTIAL | Terminal tool receipts exist; Gate V only retains provider metadata and broad run detail, hiding the decisive tool error. |
| Acceptance evidence | PARTIAL | Existing gate is useful but malformed and overclaims recovery coverage. No numerical coverage percentage is supportable. |

Spec gaps map to the child goals: monotonic policy, exact invocation identity, child lineage, decision lifecycle, reconnect/restart outcomes. The parent administration scope remains unchanged. Build health UNKNOWN for the dirty baseline; existing Gate V FAIL. No compiler or test command was run because this stage is assessment-only.

## Reference architecture lessons

Codex's local Rust source centralizes request_approval (core/src/tools/approvals.rs:495), while orchestrator.rs:125 and mcp_tool_call.rs:205 preserve independent pre-execution restrictions. Approval does not override tool disablement or host constraints. It carries a prepared invocation/catalog binding through execution (codex-mcp/src/binding.rs:169,305), rejects a stale catalog lease, and registers pending identities before emitting.

Codex stores live pending callbacks in memory (core/src/state/turn.rs:88; app-server/src/outgoing_message.rs:104). It removes them once and replays still-live requests on resume (outgoing_message.rs:362,457; request_processors/thread_lifecycle.rs:791). That proves live callback correlation, not durable approval continuation or exactly-once external writes. Remembered permission is a policy rule, not an outstanding execution receipt. Codex can transform hosted-file arguments after approval; therefore blindly copying it does not establish exact wire-argument binding.

The external harness evidence and pinned sources are in research/landscape/harness-landscape.md:
- Claude Agent SDK: host callbacks and permission modes are useful integration seams, but earlier automatic rules can skip callbacks. It is not a guarantee that every upstream Ask reaches the host.
- OpenCode: rule-based allow/ask/deny with pending deferred decisions and persisted permission rules. Persisted rules must not be mistaken for persisted pending calls.
- Gemini CLI: scheduler-owned call identity and correlation ID; explicit approval/edit/policy-update handling and cancellation. Its integrated scheduler is a pattern, not a replacement for UAR.
- Official DeepSeek Harness: distinguish approval/audit identity from gateway message identity and replay only still-live pending requests. Do not infer crash durability.
- OpenAI Agents SDK and LangGraph: serialized interruption/checkpoint continuation is an alternative for long-running workflows, with explicit resume and side-effect constraints. LangGraph may rerun code before the interrupt, so checkpointing does not imply exactly-once effects.
- AG-UI's current interrupt documentation describes ending a wire run with an interrupt outcome and starting another with a resume response. It is a protocol option, not a reason to replace UAR's logical run immediately. Current concept/draft terminology differs; pin a supported profile before adopting it.

## Candidate architectures

| Option | Fit and cost | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Repair fixture only and keep FIFO ledger | Fastest gate correction; leaves independently observed authority/identity defects | Necessary diagnostic repair, insufficient target |
| Boss owns every decision, UAR calls back | Simple desktop policy, but weakens UAR standalone and child/governance ownership | Reject as global architecture |
| UAR alone authorizes, host trusts its boolean | Fewer checks, loses Boss authority over capabilities it owns | Reject |
| UAR coordinator + explicit Boss admission | Reuses both runtimes; fixes bounded adapter/contract seams | Recommended for analyze |
| Persistent workflow/checkpoint replacement | Supports long waits but broad runtime/storage migration, does not itself solve host authorization | Defer unless a concrete product requirement needs crash continuation |
| Signed capability service / new daemon | Can serve independently deployed adversarial components, adds keys and lifecycle cost | Not justified for the current authenticated local bridge |

## Recommended contract to take into analyze

One coordinator is not one omnipotent authority. UAR owns the lifecycle and effective run policy. Boss supplies host restrictions and records decisions through an authenticated main-process adapter. Neither side can relax the other's denial or explicit human requirement. Model this as restrictive policy composition, not two unrelated prompt heuristics.

Prepare one immutable execution envelope after validation: protocol version, owner, root run, executing child run, generation/epoch, invocation ID, execution attempt, mounted server/tool/catalog revision, normalized argument representation and digest, effective policy revision, and the reason approval is required. Keep model tool-call IDs and UI request IDs distinct from the runtime's unique invocation identity. Raw secrets must not become renderer-visible digests/payloads or logs.

All host-bound calls, including Auto, traverse admission. Auto is a policy decision that still needs exact execution identity, not the absence of a ledger credit. UAR Ask requires a recorded human decision even if Boss would normally auto-approve; Boss Ask can tighten UAR Auto. Either Deny stops before dispatch. Standalone UAR uses the same coordinator with its own adapter; no new Boss dependency inside core orchestration.

The host must bind an admitted immutable envelope to the arriving execution, atomically claim it once, and recheck current host restrictions/generation. The MCP extension location or dedicated admission API remains an analyze decision: ordinary arguments cannot carry hidden permission fields, and metadata is not trustworthy just because it exists. Inspect the actual pinned rmcp API before choosing transport. A server-side opaque receipt in the existing authenticated bridge may be sufficient; signed tokens are not presumed necessary.

Proposed observable states: validated → policy denied / awaiting decision / authorized → claimed → succeeded / failed / outcome unknown. Approval decision acknowledgment and execution claim need independent idempotency. A repeated decision can report its previous result; it must not grant another execution. Cancellation/revocation before claim prevents dispatch; cancellation after dispatch does not promise rollback. An ambiguous external result is not automatically retried.

Live renderer/SSE reconnect replays the same pending record and identity, never creates a second decision or grant. For the first delivery, recommend fail-closed generation invalidation on process restart plus inspectable retained audit/result references. Clearly terminate/reconcile interrupted work; do not silently continue old approvals. This satisfies safety across restart, not transparent continuation. If “survive restart” requires continuing the pending run, durable pending records and continuation recovery become an explicit larger requirement. The analyze stage must resolve that product distinction before a plan is approved.

Use existing UAR receipts/run detail/event persistence where suitable; do not create a second database or scheduler without demonstrating the missing capability. Preserve bounded feature modules and adapter contracts for upstream mergeability. No changes to unrelated admin/Compass/Liter-LLM interfaces are needed in this child.

## Falsifiers and acceptance boundary

The architecture recommendation would need revisiting if an existing production call identity already reaches the bridge and is verified there, or host admission is actually guaranteed by a different authoritative path. No such path was found in the inspected adapter and registry. The fixture diagnosis would weaken if retained tool content from this exact run shows valid file_path arguments or a different selected schema.

At the next approved completed-functionality boundary, use the real catalog → Boss conversation → UAR → MCP → filesystem path with valid schema. Retain sanitized invocation/decision/claim/result IDs and actual failed tool content. One integration scenario set should demonstrate Ask/Auto/Deny composition, two identical calls with distinct identities, child lineage, duplicate/stale decisions, renderer and SSE reconnect separately, cancellation, generation change and outcome-unknown behavior. Prove the expected file effect and absence of unauthorized effects. Do not add per-edit unit loops or rerun a passing broad gate repeatedly. Windows x64 and macOS Apple Silicon remain equally essential release gates in the parent.

## Assessment limits and next handoff

Source review establishes concrete defects and a recommended seam, not operational correctness. Closed-source harness internals, restart guarantees, the exact prior tool-error payload, protocol extension compatibility and crash continuation requirements remain bounded unknowns. No claim of complete verification or exhaustive ecosystem coverage is made.

Analyze must settle the admission transport, envelope/canonicalization contract, policy precedence, catalog revocation semantics and restart product behavior; plan then defines coherent implementation slices and one completed integration boundary. Execution remains outside this assessment and requires the reviewed plan to be shown before proceeding.

# Unified tool approval authority

## Goal

Define a single, enforceable human-in-the-loop approval architecture for UAR runs hosted by The Boss. The architecture must preserve the effective UAR run policy, allow The Boss to impose stricter local restrictions, bind approval to the exact tool call and arguments executed by the host MCP bridge, and survive stream detach/replay, cancellation, child runs and sidecar restarts without duplicate execution or silent approval.

## Assessment questions

1. Which component owns policy resolution, approval prompting, decision recording and execution admission?
2. How are UAR `deny`, `ask` and `auto` combined with stricter Boss permission modes and built-in tool rules without either layer weakening the other?
3. What stable identifiers and lifecycle states bind an approval decision to one run, one call, one argument digest and one execution attempt?
4. How do AG-UI/SSE replay, renderer detach/reattach, cancellation, descendants and sidecar generation changes affect a pending decision?
5. Which current code paths duplicate authority or permit time-of-check/time-of-use drift?
6. What production integration boundary proves the complete contract without unit-test loops?

## Constraints

- Assessment and research only in this child until its reviewed plan is approved; no production code changes.
- UAR remains the source of the effective run policy and owns the run state machine.
- The Boss remains the user interaction host and the authority over application-owned capabilities.
- A downstream layer may tighten an upstream decision but may never weaken an explicit denial or required approval.
- No tool reaches an application-owned MCP server unless the exact call identity was admitted.
- Decisions and secrets remain main-process scoped; renderer messages carry opaque identifiers only.
- Preserve upstream-friendly seams in both repositories and the existing Agent/AG-UI contracts where they are sound.

## Exit from assessment

Produce an evidence-backed `assessment.md` with the reproduced failure, current authority/data-flow map, external architecture research, rejected alternatives, security invariants, concrete gaps, and questions the analyze/plan stages must resolve.

# Harness approval/execution landscape

Accessed: **2026-09-24**. Scope: Claude Code / Claude Agent SDK, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, and official DeepSeek Harness. Research only; no implementation, build, or behavioral test was run. Findings describe current upstream docs and source snapshots, not the versions bundled by The Boss. Codex and local UAR/Boss inspection are deliberately outside this worker's scope.

## Result

The common pattern is **runtime-owned execution with a suspended approval continuation**. This does **not** establish that a UI must be a passive yes/no renderer: Claude's public SDK explicitly permits replacement input and permission updates; Gemini supports edited content and policy changes. OpenCode and DeepSeek provide useful examples of narrower one-shot reply contracts.

Approval policy, one-shot user consent, sandbox enforcement, UI presentation, and crash recovery are distinct responsibilities. The sources do not justify collapsing all of them into a single generic boolean, nor do they prove that introducing a new central subsystem is necessary for this project.

## Version and evidence boundaries

| Product | Inspected implementation | Evidence boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Agent SDK Python | [588905686e40dffa32e2f889ce7164df01ff7c8b](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/tree/588905686e40dffa32e2f889ce7164df01ff7c8b), committed 2026-09-24 | Open-source wrapper/control transport; Claude Code engine internals were not inspected. Current TypeScript contract comes from official docs, not reverse engineering. |
| OpenCode | [6df0d5d951e0bb8c82dd1a7f9315eff4efd7f1ef](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/tree/6df0d5d951e0bb8c82dd1a7f9315eff4efd7f1ef), dev, committed 2026-09-24 | Source includes both V1 and V2. Main comparison uses V2; legacy behavior is separately labeled. This is a source revision, not an assertion of a released package version. |
| Gemini CLI | [a3d69c14200ab65d0f66f703a6c60ad644647138](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/tree/a3d69c14200ab65d0f66f703a6c60ad644647138), main, committed 2026-09-24 | Scheduler, confirmation, policy, executor, and resume UI source. Not a full security audit. |
| DeepSeek Harness | [477b4f420553e8a52c2fbccc464d7561b239c443](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/tree/477b4f420553e8a52c2fbccc464d7561b239c443), master, committed 2026-09-24 | Official developer preview; approval service, tools preparation, browser answerer, gateway continuation and documentation. APIs are explicitly evolving. |

Source files are retained as inert text snapshots under `sources/`; `source-manifest.json` records original paths, revision URLs, SHA-256 values, and retrieval dates. Official documentation snapshots include source URLs and access dates. Source claims below were statically inspected; no test result is claimed.

## Concise comparison matrix

| Question | Claude Code / Agent SDK | OpenCode V2 | Gemini CLI | DeepSeek Harness |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Who evaluates permissions? | Engine's documented hook → deny → ask → mode → allow → callback flow. SDK host decides unresolved prompts. | Core PermissionV2 evaluates configured action/resource rules and saved approvals; tool calls assert before side effects. | Core scheduler checks hooks then PolicyEngine; tools supply confirmation details. | Tools pre-execute waterfall yields allow/deny/ask; ApprovalService owns ask/never handling; later guards can still deny. |
| Who holds pending work? | Engine requests a permission decision over control transport. Python wrapper tracks handler tasks by control request ID; hidden engine's internal structure is unknown. | Location-scoped Core map holds request + Deferred. Original tool fiber awaits that Deferred. | Scheduler state holds tool call and invocation; confirmation wait matches a fresh correlationId. | Original tools continuation awaits ApprovalService; gateway holds remote-event continuation in a map; browser has only a presentation promise. |
| Identity | Control request ID and tool-use ID are distinct. TS API exposes requestId, toolUseID, optional agentID. | Permission request ID, sessionID, optional source assistant-message ID + tool-call ID. | Tool callId, confirmation correlationId, schedulerId, optional parentCallId. | Separate audit ApprovalRequestId, tool callId, agentId, transport RemoteEventId and client delivery identity. |
| Can approval change args? | Yes: documented updatedInput. | Reply API has reply/message only; no argument replacement in this contract. | Yes: inline newContent or external editor rebuilds invocation/args. | Approval request deliberately excludes args and references the already-streamed callId; shipped UI returns allowed-once/rejected. |
| Can approval change policy? | Yes: updatedPermissions with explicit settings/session destinations; mode can change separately. | always saves tool-proposed action/resource patterns for project; never overrides configured deny. | Always choices can change session policy, persist workspace/user rules, or switch edits to AUTO_EDIT. | One-shot approval outcome grants no sticky rule; separate permission presets/policy setters persist session policy. |
| Who dispatches after allow? | Engine resumes tool execution; callback returns decision, not an independent tool execution request. | Waiting runtime tool fiber continues. | Core transitions to Scheduled; scheduler executor dispatches. | Tools preparation returns dispatch only after allowed outcome, remaining guards and cancellation check. |
| UI reconnect, same process | Host application owns UI bridge; callback is an unresolved Promise. Generic UI replay contract not established by inspected SDK docs. | List/get pending requests exists; a reconnecting client can recover live pending state. | Local bus/state can present current wait; no durable remote reconnect protocol established here. | Gateway redelivers all live pending remote events to newly connected client; settled/superseded replies are no-ops. |
| Process restart | Session resume persists conversation; restoring the original pending callback/control request is not promised by the cited session contract. | Pending map/Deferred is memory; finalizer rejects on teardown. Saved rules persist in SQLite. No original continuation restoration established. | Awaiting confirmation uses memory/listeners; resume loads history/directories and chat. Original live confirmation continuation recovery not established. | Session policy/audit are durable within committed turn boundaries. Gateway continuations are memory; no pending-promise restoration established. Uncommitted turn tail handling is explicitly documented. |
| Cancel | TS callback gets AbortSignal; Python wrapper cancels in-flight task on control_cancel_request, but current Python callback context sets signal=None. | Interrupted assert cleans pending; teardown fails waiters. Reject cascades to other pending requests in same session. | Signal cancels wait; IDE/bus losing listener is aborted; user cancel cancels queued batch. | Abort settles cancelled; late answer discarded; gateway retracts pending event; only allowed-once grants. |

Sources for matrix: Claude [permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions), [user input](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input), [TS types](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#canusetool), [Python wrapper](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/588905686e40dffa32e2f889ce7164df01ff7c8b/src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/query.py); OpenCode [V2 permissions](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/permissions), [Core](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6df0d5d951e0bb8c82dd1a7f9315eff4efd7f1ef/packages/core/src/permission.ts), [HTTP handlers](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6df0d5d951e0bb8c82dd1a7f9315eff4efd7f1ef/packages/server/src/handlers/permission.ts); Gemini [scheduler](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/a3d69c14200ab65d0f66f703a6c60ad644647138/packages/core/src/scheduler/scheduler.ts), [confirmation](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/a3d69c14200ab65d0f66f703a6c60ad644647138/packages/core/src/scheduler/confirmation.ts), [policy](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/a3d69c14200ab65d0f66f703a6c60ad644647138/packages/core/src/scheduler/policy.ts); DeepSeek [approval service](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/477b4f420553e8a52c2fbccc464d7561b239c443/packages/interaction/user-approval/src/index.ts), [gateway](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/477b4f420553e8a52c2fbccc464d7561b239c443/packages/api/gateway/src/index.ts).

## Claude: useful adapter seam, not a universal policy intercept

**Verified contract.** `canUseTool` handles calls that fall through earlier permissions. Preapproved tools can bypass it. The docs recommend `PreToolUse` when a check must cover every tool call, and describe deny/ask rules that remain relevant even with hook allows and bypass mode. Do not claim that adding a central callback automatically centralizes all authorization. [Permission evaluation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions)

**Verified input/policy authority.** An allow result can carry `updatedInput` and `updatedPermissions`; permission updates can target session, user, project or local settings. The documented “always” example filters suggestions to localSettings, causing a persistent rule. A deny can return a model-visible reason; `interrupt` requests stopping the current turn. The callback can therefore be an active host decision boundary, while execution stays in the engine. [Input handling](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input), [TypeScript reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript#permissionresult)

**Verified open-source transport, limited engine claim.** Python `_spawn_control_request_handler` records tasks in `_inflight_requests[request_id]`; `control_cancel_request` cancels that task. The can_use_tool handler awaits the host callback, serializes updatedInput/updatedPermissions and sends the correlated response. This proves wrapper behavior, not hidden engine map layout, dispatch internals, or restart guarantees. The wrapper currently creates `ToolPermissionContext(signal=None)`; do not copy TypeScript AbortSignal expectations into Python without checking the shipped version. [query.py, lines 323–372 and 495–552](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/588905686e40dffa32e2f889ce7164df01ff7c8b/src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/query.py#L323)

**Restart distinction.** SDK sessions store conversation and support resume after restart. The guide separately says permission prompts are handled within a query loop. This does not promise that an old pending approval ID can be answered after a new process starts. A wrapper can persist its own UX record, but treating it as executable authorization after restart requires an explicit runtime reconciliation protocol. The latter is an adoption requirement/inference, not an SDK guarantee. [Sessions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/sessions)

**Tradeoff.** Native callback adaptation is small and retains engine semantics. Uniform interception may require hooks, and rewritten arguments make the displayed proposal/approved proposal relationship a real design decision.

## OpenCode: narrow replies and runtime continuations, with a V1/V2 trap

**Verified V2 ownership.** `PermissionV2` stores pending requests in a location-scoped map with Deferred continuations. `assert` evaluates rules, creates a request, publishes Asked, and awaits the Deferred. Its cleanup removes the request when the wait ends. Runtime teardown fails pending waiters and clears the map. Reply looks up the request ID; unknown IDs return NotFound. [Core permission.ts](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6df0d5d951e0bb8c82dd1a7f9315eff4efd7f1ef/packages/core/src/permission.ts)

**Verified reply authority.** HTTP session reply checks that the request belongs to the addressed session. The payload is reply plus optional rejection message; it does not accept replacement arguments. The server uses its stored request's suggested patterns for “always,” not patterns sent in the reply. Listing pending requests offers the building block for reconnect recovery while the runtime survives. These are interface properties, not proof that all network authentication/authorization is correct; this was not a server security audit. [Handlers](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6df0d5d951e0bb8c82dd1a7f9315eff4efd7f1ef/packages/server/src/handlers/permission.ts)

**Verified dispatch.** The V2 edit tool resolves the target, asserts external-directory permission when needed, then asserts edit permission before reading/mutating file contents. The original execution fiber continues after approval; the client does not resubmit a tool body. Source message/call IDs are passed with the permission request. [edit.ts](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6df0d5d951e0bb8c82dd1a7f9315eff4efd7f1ef/packages/core/src/tool/edit.ts)

**Verified sticky scope.** V2 “always” saves project ID + action + resource into a SQLite permission table, and saved allowances do not override configured deny. It may settle other currently pending requests whose resources become allowed, even across sessions within the location service. Reject settles other pending requests in the same session. These are deliberate broadening/cancellation scopes that an adapter should preserve or expose explicitly. [Saved service](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6df0d5d951e0bb8c82dd1a7f9315eff4efd7f1ef/packages/core/src/permission/saved.ts), [SQL](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6df0d5d951e0bb8c82dd1a7f9315eff4efd7f1ef/packages/core/src/permission/sql.ts), [Core](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6df0d5d951e0bb8c82dd1a7f9315eff4efd7f1ef/packages/core/src/permission.ts)

**Do not blend V1 and V2.** Legacy docs say “always” lasts for the current OpenCode session. The inspected legacy implementation holds approved rules in instance state, not durable storage; its exact state lifetime is more precise than that shorthand. V2 docs explicitly say durable project-scoped rules. Context7 returned examples from both generations; source and version labels resolve the apparent contradiction. [Legacy docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/), [Legacy implementation](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6df0d5d951e0bb8c82dd1a7f9315eff4efd7f1ef/packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts), [V2 docs](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/permissions)

**Tradeoff.** This is a strong model for a bounded approve/reject adapter: the runtime retains arguments, identity and continuation. It also shows that durable sticky policy and durable pending execution are separate systems.

## Gemini CLI: scheduler state machine with editable confirmation

**Verified sequence.** `_processToolCall` applies BeforeTool hooks, checks PolicyEngine, awaits confirmation if required, applies policy updates and marks the call Scheduled. `_execute` checks cancellation, marks Executing and calls the executor. The request callId is retained through those states; confirmation uses a separate correlationId. [scheduler.ts, lines 612–759](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/a3d69c14200ab65d0f66f703a6c60ad644647138/packages/core/src/scheduler/scheduler.ts#L612)

**Verified mutation authority.** Confirmation can open an external editor and loop with the new diff, or accept inline newContent. The runtime rebuilds invocation arguments through the modifier and updates scheduler state. This is an explicit counterexample to a claim that a sound approval architecture must prohibit all UI-originated input changes. It does not prove that arbitrary caller-supplied args are safe; the supported editing path is specific. [confirmation.ts](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/a3d69c14200ab65d0f66f703a6c60ad644647138/packages/core/src/scheduler/confirmation.ts), [tool-modifier.ts](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/a3d69c14200ab65d0f66f703a6c60ad644647138/packages/core/src/scheduler/tool-modifier.ts)

**Verified policy breadth.** “Always” options can mean one tool, all tools from an MCP server, persistence to workspace/user policies, or a transition to AUTO_EDIT for edit tools. Mode-scoped allowances apply to the current mode and more permissive modes. A generic “remember” flag would conceal materially different authority changes. Client-initiated tool calls can also turn ASK_USER into ALLOW, except additional-permissions requests; this is another reason to inspect every invocation path before asserting one universal prompt gate. [policy.ts](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/a3d69c14200ab65d0f66f703a6c60ad644647138/packages/core/src/scheduler/policy.ts)

**Verified cancellation, limited recovery.** Confirmation listens for the matching correlationId with AbortSignal; it races IDE and bus outcomes and cleans up the losing listener. The source explicitly calls out lost-connection/zombie-listener lifecycle responsibility. Cancel marks the call Cancelled and cancels the queued batch. Resume UI reloads conversation history, working directories and chat; it does not reconstruct the confirmation listener in the inspected path. No claim of crash-safe pending approval recovery is supported. [confirmation.ts](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/a3d69c14200ab65d0f66f703a6c60ad644647138/packages/core/src/scheduler/confirmation.ts), [resume hook](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/a3d69c14200ab65d0f66f703a6c60ad644647138/packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useSessionResume.ts)

**Tradeoff.** An explicit scheduler state model makes execution status inspectable and supports rich approval UX. Adopting its full feature set would add argument-editing and policy-scope complexity that may be unnecessary for a narrow unification task.

## DeepSeek: official harness exists; do not conflate it with the model API

The official [DeepSeek Harness developer-preview page](https://www.deepseek.com/harness/en/) links the public deepseek-ai repository and identifies models, tools, sessions, sandboxes and UI as composable plugins. This is an identifiable first-party harness as of the access date. A claim that DeepSeek has no official harness would now be false. Model function-calling support alone says nothing about this harness's permission implementation.

**Verified division of authority.** Tools runs a pre-execute waterfall; ask delegates to ApprovalService; an allowed outcome still passes monotonic guards and cancellation checks before returning dispatch. ApprovalService enforces ask/never before answerer dispatch. Missing/throwing/invalid answerers produce unavailable; only allowed-once grants. This separates the tool execution policy from the human/machine answer channel. [Tools preparation, lines 1493–1537](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/477b4f420553e8a52c2fbccc464d7561b239c443/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts#L1493), [Approval service](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/477b4f420553e8a52c2fbccc464d7561b239c443/packages/interaction/user-approval/src/index.ts)

**Verified identity and read-only question.** ApprovalService creates a fresh audit ID and records asked/decided. The request carries agent and optional callId, deliberately omitting args; UI references the streamed call. Tools snapshots and freezes execution arguments before the policy stage. Audit ID, tool-call ID and gateway transport ID serve different purposes and must not be treated as interchangeable. [Approval documentation](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/477b4f420553e8a52c2fbccc464d7561b239c443/docs/subsystems/approval.md), [Tools snapshot, lines 1391–1452](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/477b4f420553e8a52c2fbccc464d7561b239c443/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts#L1391)

**Verified reconnect building block.** Gateway stores remote waterfall continuations in pendingRemoteEvents, delivers live entries when a new client connects, and matches reply eventId to a recorded client delivery. Settlement removes the pending entry, resolves the original continuation and sends cancellation frames to other deliveries. Late/duplicate replies or replies from superseded deliveries are no-ops. Disconnect removes deliveries but leaves unresolved events available for later clients. The approval browser plugin consumes the scoped approval/request waterfall and resolves its presentation promise with a one-shot outcome. [Gateway, lines 491–660](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/477b4f420553e8a52c2fbccc464d7561b239c443/packages/api/gateway/src/index.ts#L491), [Browser answerer](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/477b4f420553e8a52c2fbccc464d7561b239c443/packages/client/ui-approval/src/client/index.ts), [Remote assembly](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/477b4f420553e8a52c2fbccc464d7561b239c443/packages/api/remotes/src/index.ts)

**Verified cancellation and limited durability.** Abort resolves the request cancelled and discards a late answer; the tools layer refuses dispatch on cancellation. Approval policy is an event-folded session override. Approval audit events require an open turn because replay uses a committed turn boundary; the source explicitly warns that bare events outside that boundary can be discarded as crash tail. The gateway continuation map is memory, and its shutdown cancels pending events. A durable audit log is therefore not evidence that the original tool continuation survives process death. [Approval service](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/477b4f420553e8a52c2fbccc464d7561b239c443/packages/interaction/user-approval/src/index.ts), [Gateway](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/477b4f420553e8a52c2fbccc464d7561b239c443/packages/api/gateway/src/index.ts)

**Verified sticky choice separation.** One-shot UI allows/rejects; separate permission presets combine sandbox mode and approval policy and persist those choices in session events. “never” means reject operations that ask, not a global deny-all. The default full-access preset can combine a broad sandbox with never prompting; capability and consent policy must be read together. [Permission presets](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/477b4f420553e8a52c2fbccc464d7561b239c443/docs/subsystems/permission-presets.md)

**Tradeoff.** Separating immutable execution from a small approval question and distinct transport identity is reusable. Adopting Cordis/plugin architecture wholesale would be an unjustified rewrite. Developer-preview source warrants careful version pinning.

## Bounded options for local assessment

These are candidate designs, not an approved architecture or claims about local defects.

| Option | What changes | Benefit | Cost / suitability boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Preserve each runtime's gate; normalize only presentation and routing | Adapter maps native approval ID + tool-call/session identity to a shared UI record and sends native outcomes back. Runtime retains its pending tool continuation. | Smallest scope; matches all four execution-ownership patterns. | Must expose real capabilities and sticky scopes per adapter; “one prompt vocabulary” does not mean one universal policy implementation. Appropriate if observed problem is duplicate/misrouted UI or argument echoing. |
| B. Runtime-owned approval broker for UAR-owned tools, native adapters for external engines | UAR's own execution path asks a central service; third-party engines continue through their native approval callbacks/hooks. UI replies by ID with allowed outcome and explicit policy scope. | Consistent UAR ownership without pretending a callback intercepts every external-engine tool. | Requires tracing actual tool paths and authority precedence; external sandbox/admin policy remains an independent deny boundary. Appropriate if observed problem is divergent UAR tool gates. |
| C. Add explicit durable approval lifecycle only if restart recovery is required | Persist proposal identity, selected policy revision and approval state; reconcile stale pending executions on restart before they can run. | Makes a promised crash/reconnect behavior reviewable. | Largest scope; a log plus ID does not resurrect a process continuation or guarantee exactly-once side effects. Sources above provide no shortcut that proves such semantics. Reject as speculative if the user requires only live-process UI reconnect. |
| D. Deliberately support approval-time edits | Explicit replacement-input operation reconstructs the runtime call and produces an auditable approved proposal. | Claude/Gemini demonstrate legitimate uses such as constrained command or diff editing. | Changes what consent authorizes; must specify display, validation and any re-evaluation behavior. Do not slip arbitrary argument echoing into a boolean reply. Unnecessary if the product does not offer editing. |

Recommended order: evaluate **A**, then **B** only where local evidence requires it; treat **C** and **D** as separate, explicit product requirements. The evidence supports runtime ownership of dispatch, but does not by itself choose a local subsystem split.

## Adversarial questions for the combined assessment

1. Does “unified authority” mean uniform UI, policy evaluation, sandbox enforcement, or execution ownership? Which observed failure requires each?
2. Is a callback actually on every execution path? Claude preapprovals and Gemini client-initiated calls are concrete counterexamples to that assumption.
3. Can one physical tool action raise multiple approval requests (external path, shell expansion, tool policy)? Tool call ID alone need not identify a particular decision.
4. Does “always” mean this process, session, project, mode, tool, server, path or user settings? The surveyed systems disagree.
5. Is the approved object the proposal shown to the user, or an edited replacement? Claude/Gemini make replacement legitimate but explicit.
6. Can a UI disconnect while the runtime keeps waiting? Does process death terminate the continuation? Do not claim restart safety based on a history log.
7. What should happen to another pending request when one is rejected or always-approved? OpenCode and Gemini have batch/session effects that a generic broker could accidentally erase.
8. Does a persistent rule revoke or override an explicit configured deny? OpenCode V2 preserves deny; “last matching wins” alone is an incomplete description of the combined policy.
9. Who reconciles stale answers, canceled requests and updated runtime generations? DeepSeek illustrates transport delivery identity in addition to tool identity.
10. Have the exact installed versions been inspected? Current docs and current main branches cannot prove a bundled older SDK's behavior.

## Search/provenance notes

- Firecrawl searches covered official docs and GitHub sources for all four families; Context7 resolved/query-docs for Claude Agent SDK, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and DeepSeek Harness.
- Firecrawl discovery found only a generic developer search provider for this task, not a structured provider containing the required cross-harness lifecycle facts. Used primary pages and pinned raw GitHub snapshots.
- One attempted DeepSeek API function-calling URL returned Page Not Found. It was not used to establish behavior.
- Primary docs/source are the evidence. Search snippets, repository issues, comments describing intended invariants, and Context7 summaries are discovery aids; no un-reproduced security issue is reported as a confirmed bug.
- Remaining uncertainties: closed-source Claude engine internals; durable pending approval reconstruction after restart; deployed-version parity; complete authn/authz of remote transports. These are intentionally not promoted into verified facts.
